claim: Karnataka cabinet (meeting of 22 Aug 2024) approved Bengaluru's first tunnel road: 18 km twin-tube corridor, Hebbal flyover to Central Silk Board, anticipated cost about Rs 12,690 crore.
who_said_it: Karnataka cabinet; announced by H.K. Patil, Law and Parliamentary Affairs Minister
exact_quote: tender processes will commence shortly
note: Cabinet note itself not seen; figure as reported by TNM. Same meeting sanctioned a Rs 500 crore sky deck.

claim: Rs 12,690 crore was the feasibility-stage twin-tube estimate for the 18.5 km Hebbal-Silk Board stretch; a single tube was estimated at Rs 11,065 crore. Feasibility consultant: Altinok Consulting Engineering (New Delhi), fee reported as Rs 5.54 crore.
who_said_it: BBMP feasibility study as reported by NBMCW / CapEx news
amount: Rs 12,690 crore (twin tube); Rs 11,065 crore (single tube); fee Rs 5.54 crore
note: Read from search excerpts only. The consultant fee is also reported elsewhere as Rs 4.7 crore. The original feasibility PDF is on data.opencity.in, which returned a Cloudflare challenge (not bypassed).

claim: BBMP released Altinok's 628-page final feasibility report ('Comprehensive Bengaluru City Traffic Management Infrastructure Plan') around 20 Dec 2024. The file on OpenCity is named for 19 Dec 2024.
who_said_it: BBMP; described by Rajkumar Dugar (Citizens for Citizens) in Citizen Matters
note: Official copy: https://data.opencity.in/dataset/6f4436f5-e3c2-4db8-a6a0-12cf0d539898/resource/305c1726-cae5-43dc-81c1-c0ae0db22c92/download/r5_final_feasibility_report_19_12_2024-compressed.pdf (Cloudflare-blocked, not read). The petitioners in WP 31626/2025 describe it as the 'December 2024 feasibility study by Altinok Consulting Engineering Pvt. Ltd.'

claim: BBMP to spend Rs 9.45 crore on the DPR alone, against the Rs 1.56 crore BMRCL spent on the Sarjapur-Hebbal metro DPR.
who_said_it: Deccan Herald report, cited by The News Minute
note: DH original (https://www.deccanherald.com/india/karnataka/bengaluru/tunnel-road-project-bbmp-to-spend-rs-9-45-cr-on-dpr-alone-3175720) returned HTTP 403. Indian Infrastructure and Construction World give Rs 950 mn / Rs 90.5 mn, which look like unit errors.

claim: The DPR contract went to Rodic Consultants after a tender in which only two bidders took part, and Rodic was reportedly the only bidder left standing.
note: So the DPR was tendered, but with effectively a single qualifying bidder. Article blocked (403); the detail comes from a search summary. Rodic was later also the sole bidder for the KR Puram-Nayandahalli tunnel DPR (Construction World). BBMP's own tender notice and award letter were not found.

claim: The DPR executive summary by Rodic is dated 24 Sep 2024 (Doc. No. DGN-1640-HO-DPR-2024/0018, Rev R0).
who_said_it: DPR document as listed on OpenCity
note: Document number taken from a search excerpt. The PDF is behind a Cloudflare challenge and was not downloaded. The court record mentions a revised DPR of February 2025.

claim: BBMP finalised the DPR in about three months: 18 km, six lanes, about Rs 16,500 crore, with interchanges at Mehkri Circle, Race Course Road and Lalbagh. PPP with about 70% private funding.
note: This verifies the Rs 16,500 crore figure as the DPR-stage estimate (Nov 2024), excluding land acquisition per DH. DH 'BBMP tunnel road DPR out in just 3 months' (3263568) was blocked.

claim: The state Finance Department agreed (3 Dec 2024) to stand guarantor for a Rs 19,000 crore BBMP loan for the tunnel road(s). BBMP planned to provide Rs 6,500 crore as viability gap funding (VGF) on a Rs 16,500 crore project.
who_said_it: Karnataka Finance Department, per Deccan Herald
amount: Rs 19,000 crore loan guarantee; Rs 6,500 crore VGF
note: DH blocked (403); details from search excerpts. BBMP issued an EOI to lenders on 6 Dec 2024 (TNIE via Magzter). TNM reported that nine banks showed interest.

claim: The 2025-26 state budget said the government stood as guarantor to BBMP for Rs 19,000 crore for the North-South and East-West tunnel roads (about 40 km, Rs 40,000 crore).
who_said_it: CM Siddaramaiah's budget speech, reported by Mongabay
amount: Rs 19,000 crore guarantee; Rs 40,000 crore for 40 km
note: The date given is the budget day as commonly reported; the budget speech PDF was not read. Whether HUDCO was the lender: one Deccan Herald report says B-SMILE planned to raise its share as a HUDCO loan. No loan sanction letter was found.

claim: Proposed toll: Rs 16/km in the feasibility report (about Rs 300 per trip), raised in the DPR to Rs 19.42/km.
who_said_it: Feasibility report and DPR, as reported by Citizen Matters and Scroll/Mongabay
amount: Rs 16/km; Rs 19.42/km; about Rs 288-330 per full trip
note: DH headline 'Rs 19/km: Bengaluru's tunnel road toll goes up even before take-off' (3596019) and 'Rs 288 for 18 km' (3331192). Final concession toll schedule not seen.

claim: Cabinet (22 May 2025) approved the 16.7 km North-South tunnel (Esteem Mall, Hebbal to Central Silk Board) at Rs 17,780 crore, with a global tender, hybrid or BOOT model to be finalised, in two phases, to be completed in three years.
who_said_it: Karnataka cabinet; D.K. Shivakumar (then Deputy CM); H.K. Patil
note: Also PTI via The Week 22 May 2025: https://www.theweek.in/wire-updates/national/2025/05/22/mds21-ka-cabinet-decisions.html. DH later reported 'BOOT model approved for tunnel road project' (3573662, blocked).

claim: B-SMILE floated the global tender (notification dated 14 Jul 2025): 16.745 km, Rs 17,698 crore excluding GST, two packages of 8.748 km each (Rs 8,770 crore Hebbal-Race Course/Seshadri Road; Rs 8,928 crore Race Course-Silk Board), BOOT, 34-year concession including 50 months of construction, EMD Rs 44.64 crore.
note: Tender date confirmed by LiveLaw (petitioners challenge 'the tender notification dated July 14, 2025'). The KPPP notice itself was not retrieved. Concession length is reported as 34 years (CW) and as 30+10 years (South First).

claim: The bid deadline was revised twice. A pre-bid query and reply document is dated 31 Oct 2025.
note: Pre-bid PDF: https://data.opencity.in/dataset/c56973c8-fe30-45e8-a0cf-b97d954f6db4/resource/f83f7097-2e91-4e62-95e4-d52652bae852/download/prebid-query-and-reply-31.10.2025.pdf (blocked; not read).

claim: Four firms bid: Adani Enterprises, Dilip Buildcon, Vishwa Samudra Engineering and Rail Vikas Nigam Ltd (RVNL).
note: DH headline 'Adani, RVNL among four firms bid for Rs 17,800 cr Bengaluru tunnel road project' (3796147).

claim: Technical stage: Dilip Buildcon was disqualified under a clause barring firms with a history of bridge, flyover or tunnel collapse. RVNL was eliminated because its JV partner failed technical criteria. Two firms reached the financial stage: Adani (L1) and Vishwa Samudra (L2; amount not reported).
who_said_it: B-SMILE bid evaluation, reported by DH and carried by TNM/IANS
note: Vishwa Samudra's quoted amounts were not found in any source.

claim: Adani Enterprises was L1 on both packages, quoting Rs 22,267 crore for the whole project against the Rs 17,698 crore estimate: about 24% above on Package 1 and 28% above on Package 2.
who_said_it: B-SMILE financial bid opening, per DH / TNM
exact_quote: the bids quoted by the conglomerate are significantly higher than the government's cost estimates
amount: Rs 22,267 crore bid vs Rs 17,698 crore estimate (gap about Rs 4,569 crore)
note: Package-wise Adani amounts are not published in any source found. The quote is TNM's wording citing DH. South First (30 Jun 2026) rounds the bid to Rs 22,000 crore.

claim: Then-Deputy CM Shivakumar said the state would fund only 40% of the estimated cost, regardless of the bid amount.
note: DH blocked; only the headline and an excerpt were seen. Consistent with TNM (Dec 2025): 'The government funds 40%'.

claim: B-SMILE sent the bid file to the state government on 29 May 2026. In mid-May, bidders were allowed to survey and soil-test along the route.
who_said_it: B-SMILE officials, per The News Minute
exact_quote: Adani was still the lowest bidder.
note: The Federal (1 Jun 2026, citing Economic Times) says Adani Enterprises was doing survey/soil testing while its bid awaited first-level clearance.

claim: D.K. Shivakumar was sworn in as Chief Minister on 3 Jun 2026. The tunnel bid needs cabinet approval because the quoted value exceeds the permissible variation from the approved estimate.
exact_quote: transform mobility
note: The quote is Shivakumar on the project.

claim: Options before the CM were to negotiate, re-estimate or re-tender. The government's estimate was revised at tender opening (Dec 2025) to a Total Concession Value of about Rs 17,800 crore; the initial figure was about Rs 14,000 crore (Rs 8,000 crore construction plus Rs 6,000 crore maintenance). Bidder assumptions: ROI 16% vs government 14% (about Rs 500 crore more), risk insurance about Rs 1,000 crore over the government figure, and maintenance more than double. VGF is capped at about 40% of construction. Concession is 30 years, extendable by 10, plus commercial rights at five 'golden exits'.
who_said_it: Unnamed CMO source, government stakeholder and Finance Department official, via South First
exact_quote: Adani [Enterprises] won the bid legitimately and government cannot indulge in favouritism or ill will
amount: TCV about Rs 17,800 crore; bid about Rs 22,000 crore
note: The article also says the bid is 'more than 90 percent higher' than the TCV, which its own figures do not support (about 24%). A Finance official said: 'At the current government estimate, no firm will take up a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) project of this scale.'

claim: Per internal documents seen by DH, the bid was up to 95.77% above the project's original benchmark and about 25% above the revised estimate. The government argued the overall premium reduces to about 35-40% against updated costs and market rates.
amount: 95.77% over original benchmark; about 25% over revised estimate; govt says 35-40%
note: DH blocked (403); figures from search excerpts only. The 'original benchmark' is probably the about Rs 14,000 crore / Rs 11,000-12,690 crore early figure, but not confirmed. R. Ashoka cites the '96% tender premium'.

claim: Gautam Adani met CM Shivakumar at his Sadashivanagar residence on 23 Aug 2026, while the Rs 22,267 crore bid was pending. The CMO called it a courtesy call.
note: Deccan Chronicle: 'DK Shivakumar dubs Adani meeting courtesy call by businessman'.

claim: Minister Priyank Kharge defended the meeting, saying the government sees Adani as a contractor and has not influenced the tender.
exact_quote: We have not influenced the tender process. Anyone can emerge as L1.
note: Same article: 'What is wrong with meeting the Chief Minister? For us, he is a contractor.'

claim: As of 1 Oct 2026 the contract had not been awarded. The CM asked the Defence Minister to release 2 acres of Hebbal Defence Dairy Farm land for a ramp; a Board of Officers order of 29 Jul 2026 sought 33% of land cost (about Rs 61 crore), and the CM proposed 2%.
exact_quote: The contract has not yet been awarded.
note: Latest dated source that confirms the contract was not yet awarded.

claim: According to the cabinet agenda, a committee would negotiate the tender rates for the two packages with the L1 bidder.
source_date: 2026-10 (search tool indicated about 34 days before 18 Nov 2026)
note: DH blocked (403). The headline 'Karnataka government to negotiate with Adani over tunnel road cost' and the agenda line come from search excerpts. The cabinet decision, committee members and any negotiated price are NOT confirmed.

claim: On 9 Sep 2026 the CM said he had asked Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda to study alternatives to Lalbagh land. The original plan needs about 6 acres of Lalbagh temporarily and 1 acre permanently.
exact_quote: look at the feasibility of alternatives to Lalbagh land for the tunnel road project
note: DH (4143729) notes the TBM shaft needs at least 5 acres and the corridor overlaps the planned Hebbal-Sarjapur metro (Red Line).

claim: After a helicopter inspection, the CM said there is a large pit near Lalbagh on the tunnel's path and that officials were told to prepare an alternative arrangement.
exact_quote: officials have been told to prepare an alternative arrangement so that there is no problem.
note: Smaller outlet. The article does not report tender status.

claim: Status as of newest sources (to 18 Nov 2026): contract NOT awarded. A negotiation with L1 Adani Enterprises was reportedly put on the cabinet agenda in October 2026. The Lalbagh alignment is being re-examined. The PILs are pending, and any contract is subject to their outcome.
who_said_it: Compiled from CW 1 Oct 2026, DH Oct 2026, TNM 10 Sep 2026, LiveLaw 16 Jul 2026
note: No source after mid-October 2026 on the negotiation outcome was found. The Hindu and Indian Express could not be searched (blocked to this tool).

claim: Not to be confused: the separate Hebbal 'short tunnel' / Mehkri Circle-Hebbal integrated corridor (BDA). Cabinet approved Rs 2,215 crore for the tunnel plus elevated corridor; the CM said on 10 Nov 2026 it should be ready in 18 months; Ballari Road curbs ran from 6 Nov 2026.
note: Separate project. The Finance Department's objections to cost and effectiveness were reported for THIS short tunnel, not the 16.75 km tunnel.

claim: Earlier and larger proposals: a 190 km tunnel network was floated; Altinok proposed 54.5 km of tunnels at about Rs 32,700 crore; BBMP's June 2024 18 km proposal was about Rs 8,043-8,100 crore (about Rs 450 crore/km).
who_said_it: D.K. Shivakumar / BBMP / Altinok, per TNM, DH, Indian Infrastructure
amount: Rs 8,043 crore (Jun 2024); Rs 32,700 crore for 54.5 km
note: The exact date of the first announcement was NOT confirmed. TNM 'A 190-km tunnel road proposed for Bengaluru traffic' (https://www.thenewsminute.com/karnataka/a-190-km-tunnel-road-proposed-for-bengaluru-traffic-disaster-in-the-making) is undated in what was seen. An unnamed TNM source (Sep 2024) said the concept 'was primarily brought up by various builders during Brand Bengaluru meetings' (anonymous; not verified).

claim: An expert committee appointed by the Urban Development Department, headed by Siddanagouda Hegaraddi (Executive Director, Civil, BMRCL), found the DPR hastily prepared. Findings: only four soil test points; no field traffic survey; traffic study 'particularly weak'; alignment nearly parallel to the metro north-south corridor; Lalbagh shaft should be reconsidered; ramps could worsen congestion at Palace Grounds and Mehkri Circle; demand projected only to 2041; data supports 2+2 rather than 3+3 lanes.
exact_quote: particularly weak
note: Committee report: https://data.opencity.in/dataset/35996dfd-6dd9-4eac-8b53-caec0ae82878/resource/2351a5e8-5f08-41b7-b53e-22b08a4092fa/download/hegaraddi-committee-main-report.pdf (403/Cloudflare; NOT read). Reportedly constituted April 2025.

claim: The committee devoted nearly 50 pages of an 89-page report to 121 shortcomings in the Rs 9.5 crore DPR, and listed nine missing 'important elements': land acquisition plan, tree enumeration and relocation, EIA, social impact assessment, and a disaster management and security plan, among others. After a second review, the committee replied on 27 May (2025) that it was still not convinced.
who_said_it: UDD expert committee, per Deccan Herald and South First
note: The 121 figure and the 27 May date are from DH 'Subterranean shock' (3791668), blocked; seen only via search excerpts. South First confirms the nine elements and the four soil points. The government reportedly stayed 'firm on going ahead'.

claim: DULT (secretariat of BMLTA) reviewed the feasibility report and sent comments in Nov 2024, warning the tunnel contradicted the Comprehensive Mobility Plan and Climate Action Plan. BBMP commissioned the DPR before the BMLTA review was complete. DULT later said its remarks should not be construed as BMLTA's opinion.
who_said_it: DULT; Sathya Arikutharam (mobility expert) linking it to the committee findings
exact_quote: should not be construed as the opinion of BMLTA
note: DH 'After scathing review, DULT dilutes objection to tunnel road project' (3686542) blocked. ThePrint (4 Nov 2025) reports that three government agencies reportedly opposed the project and later allegedly diluted their findings (attributed to critics).

claim: A GSI committee report (submitted to government in April 2026) warned that drill-and-blast for the TBM shaft near the Lalbagh Geological Monument could fracture or destabilise the Peninsular Gneiss; called Shaft 4 a 'critical concern' needing independent review of its location; warned of groundwater effects on Lalbagh lake; found the DPR's surface investigation inadequate; and recommended comprehensive geotechnical study and possibly 3D modelling.
who_said_it: Geological Survey of India expert committee
exact_quote: could induce rock fractures or destabilise parts of the formation
note: The GSI report itself was not seen. South First headline: 'DK Shivakumar says tunnel road project poses no risk to Lalbagh; geotechnical report says otherwise.'

claim: BBMP penalised Rodic Consultants after the DPR executive summary referred to Malegaon and Nashik (Maharashtra) while analysing Bengaluru corridors. BBMP said the error crept in when the executive summary was compiled, not in the draft DPR, and that the consultants acknowledged it and apologised.
amount: Rs 5 lakh (CW, Citizen Matters) or Rs 10 lakh (DH headline): conflicting
note: The penalty amount conflicts: DH 'BBMP slaps Rs 10 lakh penalty on tunnel road consultant' (3389674) vs Rs 5 lakh elsewhere. The penalty order was not seen. Citizen Matters (12 Feb 2025) places a Rs 5 lakh penalty on the 'consultant over errors' (it may refer to the feasibility consultant; ambiguous).

claim: The SEIAA Karnataka communication of 26 Nov 2024 stated that prior environmental clearance was not required. The DPR says no EIA is required.
who_said_it: SEIAA Karnataka (as cited in the PIL); DPR (as reported by Mongabay)
note: Challenged by petitioners. B-SMILE told the press (CW 2 Mar 2026) that an EIA has been completed for the Lalbagh-area alignment with an environmental management plan; this needs reconciling.

claim: In a written reply to MLC C.T. Ravi in the Legislative Council, Shivakumar said the tunnel road could need about 80 acres per the DPR, close to 80% of it government land.
who_said_it: D.K. Shivakumar (Deputy CM), written answer, Legislative Council
note: DH blocked; from search excerpt. The council record itself was not located.

claim: In the Council, Shivakumar called the tunnel road 'the only option' and said its cost is about Rs 770 crore/km versus Rs 1,316 crore/km for two other tunnels he cited.
exact_quote: the only option
note: DH blocked; from search excerpt. Which two tunnels were compared is not confirmed. Rs 770/km does not match the tender (Rs 17,698 cr / 16.745 km = about Rs 1,057/km); it may use construction cost only.

claim: The Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) (Amendment) Bill, 2026, allowing up to 5% of park land to be used for public projects, passed the legislature on 24 Aug 2026 without substantive debate. After protests linking it to the Lalbagh tunnel shaft, the cabinet decided to withdraw it (about 3 Sep 2026) and to reintroduce a reworked version after public consultation.
who_said_it: Karnataka legislature / cabinet; Parliamentary Affairs Minister G. Parameshwara
note: Critics alleged the bill was meant to divert Lalbagh land; the government did not say so. Tejasvi Surya called the withdrawal a 'temporary victory'.

claim: No CAG audit paragraph on the tunnel road was found.
note: Expected, since no expenditure beyond studies has occurred. CAG site not searched directly.

claim: PILs WP 31626/2025 c/w WP 28664/2025 (Prakash Belawadi and Dr Adikesavalu Ravindra v. State of Karnataka) challenge the 14 Jul 2025 tender notification, RFP, pre-bid, bid evaluation and proposed LoA; the Altinok feasibility study; the Rodic DPR and its Feb 2025 revision; and the SEIAA 26 Nov 2024 no-EC communication. Ground: statutory procedures (EIA, BMLTA) were bypassed.
note: LiveLaw is partly paywalled. A connected PIL (Akshay Vasist, Vasista Ramprasad and others) is listed; a further PIL argues there was no hydrological or groundwater or lake study.

claim: Oct 2025 hearings before CJ Vibhu Bakhru and Justice C.M. Poonacha: the court asked whether Lalbagh trees would be felled. The State told the court that no trees inside Lalbagh would be cut till the next hearing, and the matter was adjourned to 9 Dec 2025.
note: The outcome of the 9 Dec 2025 hearing was not found.

claim: BJP MP Tejasvi Surya filed a PIL against the North-South tunnel road. He mentioned it before the Chief Justice on 29 Jun 2026, and it was listed for 6 Jul 2026.
exact_quote: I requested the Hon'ble Chief Justice for a short date.
note: Case number not found. Grounds not stated in the report.

claim: Interim order of 16 Jul 2026 (CJ Vibhu Bakhru and Justice K.S. Hemalekha): the State must ensure no equities are created; the pendency of the petitions is to be communicated to third parties and contractors; any contract is subject to the outcome; notice issued on the PIL against Rule 24 of the BMLTA Rules, 2026. Next hearing 20 Aug 2026.
exact_quote: Any such contract would be subject to the outcome of this petition.
note: Also recorded: 'ensure that no equities are created'. The court said it was not endorsing the State's solution, adding: 'if there are some rules or regulations to be followed, you are free to point out.' The order copy itself was not retrieved.

claim: Petitioners' Senior Counsel argued the State skipped the impact study and called it a real estate project. The petitioners said they do not oppose the project itself, only the bypassing of procedure. The AG (Shashi Kiran Shetty) opposed.
who_said_it: Arun Kumar, Senior Counsel for petitioners
exact_quote: This is not a road project... but a real estate project.
note: Advocacy in court, not a finding.

claim: The High Court directed the authorities to place the GSI report on the Lalbagh Peninsular Gneiss before it, and asked the State for an engineer's presentation on whether the shorter tunnel beneath Hebbal Lake could affect inflow, outflow and underground flow. Reportedly posted to 10 Sep 2026.
who_said_it: Karnataka High Court (CJ Vibhu Bakhru, Justice K.S. Hemalekha)
exact_quote: directed the authorities to place before it the Geological Survey of India's (GSI) report
note: The hearing day is inferred as Thursday 3 Sep 2026 from the 4 Sep publication. The 10 Sep date is from a search summary. Proceedings after 10 Sep 2026 and the current next date were NOT found.

claim: Citizen groups petitioned the National Green Tribunal to declare the project unlawful.
note: NGT case number and status not found.

claim: B-SMILE says the project is 'completely data-driven', will follow NGT norms, and that 4,168 pages of records were submitted to the High Court.
exact_quote: completely data-driven approach
note: CW mis-expands the B-SMILE acronym in this article.

claim: Tejasvi Surya called the project 'vanity' and 'unscientific'. He said it costs more than the Atal Tunnel, more per km than the Mumbai Coastal Road, and more than the 655 km Thiruvananthapuram-Kasaragod highway. He cited a Rs 7,100 crore VGF need, a proposed Rs 660 toll, and the absence of the BMLTA approval required under Sec 19 of the BMLTA Act.
exact_quote: unscientific
amount: VGF Rs 7,100 crore; toll Rs 660 (as claimed)
note: PTI. Claims, not verified. The Rs 660 toll is probably a round trip, not confirmed.

claim: Surya, citing the DPR and IISc data, said the tunnel moves about 1,800 vehicles per hour per direction versus about 69,000 people for a metro. He also said tunnel roads 'merely shift traffic from one junction to another'.
exact_quote: Tunnel roads do not decongest cities; they merely shift traffic from one junction to another.

claim: Shivakumar replied that scrapping the tunnel for public transport is not feasible without Union funds, and that Surya offered no workable alternative.
note: Headline: 'Funds, not advice, needed'.

claim: Shivakumar said the tunnel is a public initiative, not his personal project, and that Union Minister Nitin Gadkari backed it.
exact_quote: The Tunnel Road is not my personal project - it's a public initiative for Bengaluru's future.
note: Also: 'I'm not a fool to destroy Lalbagh.'

claim: Government claims of benefit: the tunnel lets commuters skip 25 traffic bottlenecks and cut travel time from about 90 to 45 minutes (Shivakumar on X). The DPR says the corridor's 90 minutes falls to 35 minutes. Underground roads avoid land acquisition and demolition.
exact_quote: can help commuters skip 25 traffic bottlenecks
note: DPR 90 to 35 min per Scroll (10 Nov 2025). ThePrint: the DPR claims Hebbal to Vidhana Soudha time is halved from about 30 min. Also Shivakumar: 'If I touch Lalbagh, the citizens will break my head.'

claim: Leader of Opposition R. Ashoka (BJP) called the project a 'money-making business' and the tender 'scandalous' and 'inflated'. He sought cancellation over the 96% premium, about 40 years of toll, and allotment of prime land to the concessionaire, and accused the government of a double standard on Adani.
who_said_it: R. Ashoka, Leader of Opposition, BJP
exact_quote: Congress opposes Adani in Delhi, but supports him in Karnataka. Isn't this a double standard?
note: The quote is from South First, 24 Aug 2026. The DH article was blocked; the 'money-making business' line is from ANI/Asianet, 15 Nov 2025. These are allegations.

claim: BJP MP P.C. Mohan opposed the cabinet approval.
exact_quote: Bengaluru needs India's Metro, not Turkey's tunnel.
note: 'Turkey' refers to Altinok's origin.

claim: IISc IST Lab simulation: the tunnel would carry about 1,200 passengers per hour per direction versus about 69,000 for a nine-car metro of the same cost. Relief would be temporary because of induced traffic (about 3,000 new registrations a day). There is a flood-entrapment risk underground.
who_said_it: Prof. Ashish Verma, IISc Sustainable Transportation Lab
exact_quote: Underground, you can get totally trapped. Think of the extreme stress that people will face.
note: Verma, TNM 9 Sep 2024: 'The cost of building a road tunnel is much higher than that of a metro tunnel.'

claim: The IISc lab projected that the tunnel shifts mode share toward private vehicles: MRTS 43.5% falling to 42.2% by 2041, and public plus non-motorised transport 81.9% falling to 75.6%.
Hydrogeologists say the DPR considered only surface conditions; the alignment passes through soft saprolite zones that could disturb aquifers and drainage.
who_said_it: G.V. Hegde and K.C. Subhash Chandra, hydrogeologists
note: Counterview: HSM Prakash (retired GSI) told Mongabay the rock beneath Lalbagh is 'a compact, massive rock' and a tunnel at 60 m depth should not be a problem (Scroll/Mongabay, Nov 2025).

claim: Mobility expert: no transport-planning need for the tunnel; risk to groundwater.
exact_quote: There is no need for such an infrastructure from a transport planning perspective.
note: Also: 'It is scandalous to mess with the groundwater situation in Bengaluru.'

claim: Citizens for Citizens: about 90% of the tunnel lies within 1 km of planned metro stations; 16 ramps add about 2.23 km per trip; a toll of about Rs 300 per trip exceeds fuel cost and would deter use; vehicle data is outdated; the project is not in the CMP and there has been no public consultation. A ventilation shaft in Lalbagh would act like a 'chimney'.
who_said_it: Rajkumar Dugar, founder, Citizens for Citizens (C4C)
exact_quote: The tunnels are largely redundant due to existing and planned metro lines and suburban rail projects.
note: The 'chimney' ventilation remark is per South First, 15 Oct 2025. Ventilation was otherwise not found addressed in any official source.

claim: Other attributed criticism: tunnels add road space that induces car buying (Bengaluru Bus Prayanikara Vedike); the money could build more footpaths, buses and cycle tracks (Ashwin Mahesh); the vision is a real estate developer's (historian Janaki Nair); 'misplaced priority' (Bengaluru Bus Travellers' Forum).
who_said_it: Vinay Sreenivasa; Ashwin Mahesh; Janaki Nair; Shaheen Shasa
exact_quote: Tunnels only add more road space, which will encourage people to buy more cars.
note: Ashwin Mahesh in ThePrint 4 Nov 2025; Shasa in Mongabay Mar 2025.

claim: Bengaluru Praja Vedike said it would keep opposing the project even if Lalbagh is excluded from the alignment.
note: DH blocked; from search excerpt. No statements by Bengaluru Navanirmana Party (BNP) or JD(S) were found in the sources reached.

claim: Surya alleged the tunnel DPR (Rs 9.5 crore) copied data from BMRCL's Rs 1.6 crore DPR and pointed to the Malegaon/Nashik references. He also alleged that a group company of the feasibility consultant formed a JV with a firm debarred in Madhya Pradesh on an NHAI project, and that the DPR consultants were involved in a Rs 500 crore 'scam' in Jammu and Kashmir.
note: ALLEGATIONS ONLY. No debarment order, no J&K case record and no plagiarism finding was located. The only record-backed 'copying' item is BBMP's acknowledgement of the Malegaon/Nashik error plus the penalty. No response from Altinok or Rodic was found.

claim: The tender lets the concessionaire develop commercially at five intermodal hub and shaft sites ('golden exits', about 6 acres in total); foundations are designed for 5 basements + ground + 15 storeys. B-SMILE says the commercial component is optional and buildings return to the state at the end of the concession.
who_said_it: Tender documents per DH; B-SMILE officials
exact_quote: The bidder is expected to return the building after the concession period.
note: Original DH report (3776133) blocked. This is the record basis for critics' 'real estate project' framing; the RFP itself was not read.
